subtitle: How chauth, coins and ledgers bound a cavalry power into a fiscal empire

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of a court scene fading into a map of India
panels.action: Shahu I stands in royal posture in a dim Satara court, one hand resting on a scroll while behind him a ghostly map of the subcontinent glows, threaded with faint routes and coins, suggesting an unseen fiscal web.

dialogue.text: Shahu I and his revenue officers weave chauth, sardeshmukhi and coins into a new kind of Maratha sovereignty across a crumbling empire.

i18n.hi: शाहू और उनके महसूल अफसर चौथ, सरदेशमुखी और सिक्कों से बिखरते साम्राज्य में नई मराठा हुकूमत बुनते हैं।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot overlooking the Deccan from a hilltop
panels.action: From a rocky hill near Satara, Shahu I, older and thoughtful, looks out over a hazy Deccan plain dotted with forts, villages and distant Mughal camps, his cloak tugged by the wind.

dialogue.text: By the early 1700s, cannons and cavalry had shaken the Mughal giant. Yet power in India still flowed through land, taxes and the quiet ink of accountants.

i18n.hi: 1700 के शुरू में तोपें और घुड़सवार मुगल दैत्य को हिला चुके थे, पर असली ताकत अभी भी जमीन, लगान और खामोश मुनीमों की स्याही से बहती थी।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of Shahu in durbar surrounded by scribes
panels.action: Inside the Satara durbar, Shahu I sits on a modest throne while revenue officers and Modi-script scribes kneel with bundles of worn papers, some pointing at figures, others waiting anxiously.

dialogue.text: Shahu, grandson of Shivaji, returned from Mughal captivity to a kingdom of brave horsemen and fragile ledgers. The sword had opened space; the pen had to hold it.

i18n.hi: शिवाजी के पोते शाहू, मुगल क़ैद से लौटे तो घोड़ेसवार वीर थे, पर बहीखाते नाज़ुक। तलवार ने जगह बनाई थी, कलम को उसे संभालना था।

panels.shot: close-up on a Modi-script ledger and a pointing hand
panels.action: A calloused officer’s hand traces columns in a Modi-script ledger spread on a low desk, with headings marked for chauth shares and sardeshmukhi, small piles of coins placed beside each column.

dialogue.text: From these ledgers grew the Maratha fiscal state: chauth on imperial lands, sardeshmukhi as chief’s claim, and careful division between king, officers and troops.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं बहीखातों से मराठा खजाना-राज बना—मुगल जमीनों पर चौथ, सरदेशमुखी मुखिया का हक, और राजा, अफसर, फौज के बीच नाप-तोल से बँटी आमदनी।

panels.shot: diagrammatic bird’s-eye showing Deccan districts with superimposed faint lines
panels.action: A bird’s-eye view of Deccan districts, stylized like a map: villages, rivers and main roads are faintly overlaid with lines and small coin symbols following the paths toward Satara and Pune.

dialogue.text: Chauth was not mere tribute. It was a claim to a share of land revenue—of one-fourth in many regions—asserted over Mughal districts from Gujarat to the Narmada.

i18n.hi: चौथ सिर्फ नजराना नहीं था, जमीन के लगान में हिस्सा था—कई सूबों में एक-चौथाई—जो गुजरात से नर्मदा तक मुगल जिलों पर जताया गया।

panels.shot: interior wide of Mughal court with Maratha envoy low in the frame
panels.action: In a resplendent Mughal hall, a Maratha envoy bows before a distant emperor’s throne while Persian scribes record terms, a faint outline of a farman scroll highlighted between them.

dialogue.text: In 1719, amidst palace intrigues in Delhi, a Mughal farman recognized Maratha rights to chauth and sardeshmukhi in parts of the Deccan, turning pressure into imperial legality.

i18n.hi: 1719 में, दिल्ली की कचहरी साज़िशों के बीच, एक मुगल फ़रमान ने दक्खन के हिस्सों में मराठों की चौथ और सरदेशमुखी मान ली—दबाव को ही बादशाही क़ानून बना दिया।

panels.shot: medium shot of Shahu receiving a scroll from a courier
panels.action: Back in Satara, a dust-covered courier kneels, offering the sealed farman to Shahu I; the king’s eyes narrow as he holds the scroll between nervous officers and hopeful scribes.

dialogue.speaker: shahu_i_and_the_maratha_revenue_officers
dialogue.text: Now the emperor himself writes our share into his land.

i18n.hi: अब खुद बादशाह ही हमारी हिस्सेदारी अपनी जमीन में लिख रहा है।

panels.shot: busy interior of Peshwa office with multiple desks and scribes
panels.action: In a bustling Peshwa office at Pune, rows of Modi-script scribes bend over ledgers; a senior revenue officer stands, directing clerks who sort copper Shivrai coins and silver rupees into labeled trays.

dialogue.text: In Pune and Satara, Peshwa officers turned farmans into orders, orders into account books. Campaigns were planned not only with maps, but with columns of expected chauth.

i18n.hi: पुणे और सतारा में पेशवा के कारिंदों ने फ़रमानों को हुक्म बनाया, हुक्मों को हिशाब-किताब। अब मुहिमें सिर्फ नक्शों से नहीं, आने वाली चौथ के कॉलम से भी बनती थीं।

panels.shot: close-up of hands sealing a revenue assignment document
panels.action: A revenue officer presses a signet into wax on a folded document while a moneylender waits nearby, his fingers resting on a neat stack of hundi papers and a small box of coins.

dialogue.text: Collections were farmed out as assignments. Banking houses advanced cash on the strength of these papers, their hundis carrying Maratha credit from bazaar to battlefield.

i18n.hi: वसूली ठेकों में बाँटी गई। इन्हीं कागज़ों की ताकत पर साहूकार ने नकद उधार दिया, उनकी हुंडियाँ मराठा साख को बाज़ार से मैदान तक ले गईं।

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of Maratha cavalry riding through a dusty plain
panels.action: A long line of Maratha cavalry rides at a steady pace through a dusty Central Indian plain, a mounted revenue officer in front clutching a leather pouch heavy with documents.

dialogue.text: Beyond the Deccan, Maratha forces rode into Malwa, Gujarat and Bundelkhand. Their spears marked presence; their revenue officers marked a new fiscal claim on distant fields.

i18n.hi: दक्खन के पार मराठा टुकड़ियाँ मालवा, गुजरात, बुंदेलखंड तक दौड़ीं। भालों ने हाज़िरी दर्ज की, महसूल अफसरों ने दूर खेतों पर नया खजाना-हक।

panels.shot: medium shot of a revenue officer and local Mughal official at a table
panels.action: In a town office in Malwa, a Maratha revenue officer sits across from a wary Mughal official, both leaning over a local register while village headmen stand behind, watching tensely.

dialogue.text: In many districts, Maratha chauth did not replace the imperial state; it latched onto it, inserting an extra share into existing village registers and zamindar obligations.

i18n.hi: कई इलाकों में मराठा चौथ ने बादशाही राज को बदला नहीं, उससे चिपक गई—मौजूदा गांव-रजिस्टर और ज़मींदारों पर बस एक extra हिस्सा और दर्ज हो गया।

panels.shot: close-up on coins from different regions on a cloth
panels.action: On a rough cloth spread over a table, different coins—copper Shivrais, silver rupees with varying scripts and symbols from Pune, Nagpur, Baroda and Gwalior—are arranged in small, labeled clusters.

dialogue.text: Numismatists still trace this spread. Shivrai traditions continued, but under Shahu and his successors, new Maratha rupees appeared from Pune, Nagpur, Baroda and Gwalior, proclaiming local authority in silver.

i18n.hi: सिक्का-विद जानकार आज भी इस फैलाव को पकड़ते हैं। शिवराई चलती रही, पर शाहू और आगे के राजों में पुणे, नागपुर, बड़ौदा, ग्वालियर से नए मराठा रुपये निकले—चाँदी में अपना हक जताते हुए।

panels.shot: interior of a small mint with workers at furnaces and anvils
panels.action: Inside a modest mint, workers tend a glowing furnace, pour metal into molds and strike coin blanks with engraved dies, while an overseer compares fresh coins to a reference piece.

dialogue.text: These mints did not always erase the emperor’s name. Often, Maratha symbols and local marks shared the face of coins with fading Mughal legends, mirroring shared and contested sovereignty on the ground.

i18n.hi: इन टकसालों ने हमेशा बादशाह का नाम नहीं मिटाया। कई बार मराठा निशान और देसी मुहरें, मिटती मुगल लिखावट के साथ एक ही सिक्के पर दिखीं—जमीन पर बँटी और झगड़ती हुकूमत का चेहरा बनकर।

panels.shot: medium shot of Shahu with leading sardars and revenue officers around a floor map
panels.action: Shahu kneels by a large floor map marked with colored stones, surrounded by leading sardars and revenue officers, each stone representing a region’s chauth shares, some placed near Satara, others pushed outward.

dialogue.text: As the confederacy grew, Shahu’s court tried to hold the web together. Shares of chauth fed the central treasury, but also nourished rising houses—the Holkars, Scindias, Bhonsles and Gaekwads.

i18n.hi: संघ बढ़ा तो शाहू की दरबार ने इस जाल को जोड़े रखने की कोशिश की। चौथ के हिस्से से केंद्रीय खजाना भरता, पर साथ ही होलकर, शिंदे, भोंसले, गायकवाड़ जैसे घराने भी पलते रहे।

panels.shot: split composition showing Pune office on one side and a distant sardar court on the other
panels.action: On the left, Peshwa scribes in Pune tally columns in a dim office; on the right, a distant Maratha sardar in Malwa sits in his own court with local accountants and village petitions, mirroring the scene.

dialogue.text: Power dispersed with revenue. Subordinate Maratha houses collected chauth in their spheres, maintained their own mints and ledgers, and only part of that flow returned to Satara or Pune.

i18n.hi: ताकत भी महसूल के साथ बिखर गई। अधीन मराठा घरानों ने अपनी-अपनी हद में चौथ जुटाई, अपनी टकसालें और बहीखाते रखे, और उसका बस एक हिस्सा ही सतारा या पुणे लौटा।

panels.shot: intimate close-up of Shahu in later years reading a worn account book
panels.action: In his later years, a tired Shahu sits by lamplight, turning the pages of a worn account book, his face lined with worry as the columns of arrears and assignments lengthen.

dialogue.text: For peasants and merchants, these layers of claim could feel like burden. Scholars still debate: was this extraction, sovereignty, or the rough work of state formation in a broken empire?

i18n.hi: किसान और बनियों के लिए ये परत-दर-परत दावे बोझ जैसे लग सकते थे। आज भी बहस है—ये बस निचोड़ थी, हुकूमत थी, या टूटते साम्राज्य में नया राज्य गढ़ने की कड़ी मेहनत?

panels.shot: wide shot of an Indian bazaar with moneylenders, soldiers and peasants
panels.action: In a bustling bazaar, a moneylender writes out a hundi as Maratha soldiers wait nearby, a peasant negotiates at a grain stall, and a trader counts mixed coins into a cloth bag.

dialogue.text: Yet through hundis, assignments and coins, Maratha fiscal claims stitched together markets. Credit lines now ran from Deccan villages to Malwa towns and coastal ports.

i18n.hi: पर हुंडियों, ठेकों और सिक्कों के ज़रिए मराठा खजाना-दावे ने बाज़ारों को जोड़ा। अब साख की लकीरें दक्खन के गांवों से मालवा के कस्बों और समुंदरी बंदरों तक जाती थीं।

panels.shot: aerial view of India with lines radiating from Pune, Satara, Nagpur, Baroda, Gwalior
panels.action: An elevated map-like view of the subcontinent shows soft glows at Pune, Satara, Nagpur, Baroda and Gwalior, with fine lines of routes and coins radiating out and overlapping.

dialogue.text: By the late eighteenth century, Maratha sovereignty was less a single throne than a confederacy of fiscal nodes—each with its mints, its chauth circuits, its own bargaining with peasants and bankers.

i18n.hi: अठारहवीं सदी के आखिर तक मराठा हुकूमत एक तख्त नहीं, खजाने के कई गाठों का संघ बन चुकी थी—हर जगह अपनी टकसाल, अपनी चौथ-लकीरें, अपने किसानों और साहूकारों से सौदे।

panels.shot: final contemplative shot of a closed ledger resting atop a sheathed sword
panels.action: On a wooden table, a heavy ledger bound in leather rests atop a sheathed Maratha sword, dust motes drifting in the light from a nearby lattice window.

dialogue.text: The Maratha chauth that began as a share on imperial lands became a claim to rule. In their wake, they left a lesson: empires endure or fall as much by accounts as by arms.

i18n.hi: मुगल जमीनों पर हिस्से से शुरू हुई मराठा चौथ आख़िर राज के दावे में बदली। उनके पीछे एक सबक रह गया—साम्राज्य तलवार से जितना, खाता-बही से भी उतना टिकते या ढहते हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: How chauth, coins and ledgers bound a cavalry power into a fiscal empire
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे चौथ, सिक्के और हिशाबों ने घुड़सवार ताकत को खजाना-सम्राज्य बना दिया
